Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc-Lko:48078
Court No. - 11

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 4306 of 2023
Applicant :- Dipak Alias Ajay Kumar Gautam

Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru.Secy.Home And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Rehan Ahmad Siddiqui,Dildar Khan

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1. Heard Sri Rhan Ahmad Siddiqui and Sri Dildar Khan, learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.

No one appeared on behalf of the opposite party no.2,
despite service of notice.
2. The FIR in question was lodged alleging that the applicant used to harass the victim for about 2 years, for which, the FIR No.471 of 2020 was lodged.
It was further alleged that the photographs of the victim was uploaded on internet and on inspection, it was revealed that it was done by the applicant by making a false ID.

It was further alleged that on 07.06.2022, at about 11:00 AM, the applicant came to the house of the victim and after removing her pant, insert the finger in private Dipak Alias Ajay Kumar Gautam vs State Of U.P. sentences.text:
Similar statements were made in the statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C.
3.
The Counsel for the applicant argues that the FIR in question was false, inasmuch as, there was a history of litigation in the family as disclosed in the FIR itself.
It is further argued that a Challani report was lodged on account of altercation and scuffle took place in between the parties.
The Challani report is dated 08.06.2022 whereas the incident is said to have occurred on 07.06.2022.
He argues that there is no mention of the alleged incident in the Challani report.
The FIR in question was lodged on 13.06.2022.
4. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer.

5. Considering the history of ligation in between the families as disclosed in the FIR itself coupled with the fact that the applicant is in custody since 24.11.2022 and even the charge has not been framed coupled with the fact that the applicant does not have any criminal antecedents, there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
6.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Dipak @ Ajay Kumar Gautam be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.207 of 2022, under Section 376 IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, Section 66E of IT Act, Police Station Raniganj, District Pratapgarh on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
